description: Takımımız, Ay ve Mars yüzeyinde terk edilmiş tarihi uzay araçlarından elde edilen telemetry verilerini modern analiz ve hikayeleştirme teknikleriyle birleştirerek, bu sessiz anıtların kayıp hikayelerini açığa çıkarmayı ve geleceğe aktarmayı hedeflemektedir. Verilerin sessiz tanıklığını sesli bir mirasa dönüştürmek için buradayız.
summary:
Telemetry Tales is an interactive web platform that transforms technical archive data from 13 pioneering spacecraft left behind on the Moon, Mars, and deep space during NASA's historic space missions from the 1960s to the present (Apollo 11, Apollo 12, Apollo 15, Surveyor Landers, Sojourner Rover, Spirit & Opportunity, Viking 1 & 2 Landers, Phoenix & InSight Landers, Ingenuity Helicopter, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer 10 & 11, Kepler Space Telescope, and Dawn Spacecraft) into an immersive digital museum experience for secondary school students and young science enthusiasts.

The project combines open-access yet complex technical archive data from sources such as NSSDCA with first-person stories narrated from an "I" perspective, real mission photographs, planetary filtering tabs (Moon / Mars / All), bilingual interface support (English/Turkish), and live telemetry simulations, transforming cold engineering records into living monuments with which young people can form an emotional and scientific connection.
details: Telemetry Tales is an interactive digital museum platform designed to introduce younger generations to the stories and technical features of 13 pioneering spacecraft left on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space during NASA’s historical missions. Our project transforms NASA’s publicly available but technically complex archival data into an engaging, visual, and story-driven experience that everyone can understand. Users can explore spacecraft through Moon and Mars filters and access real mission photographs, technical specifications, and first-person narratives told from each spacecraft’s perspective. Additionally, bilingual support (Turkish and English), detailed information windows, and live telemetry simulations displaying parameters such as signal strength, communication delays, and surface temperature allow users to explore space missions more closely. The main purpose of our project is to increase young people’s interest in space science, preserve the scientific legacy of past missions, and demonstrate how today’s discoveries are built upon previous engineering achievements. During development, we used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to create a web-based prototype, while GitHub was used for code management and publishing the website. We collected scientific information from NASA’s open-access resources, including NSSDCA, the Planetary Data System, and Solar System Exploration. Our three-member creative team considered several factors, including scientific accuracy, the target audience’s age and interests, user experience, visual design, accessibility, and bilingual usability. The innovative aspect of our project lies in giving forgotten spacecraft a unique narrative identity by allowing them to tell their own stories and transforming technical engineering data into an interactive experience that encourages emotional connection. Therefore, Telemetry Tales is not simply a platform introducing historical space missions; it is also a digital scientific heritage project that aims to inspire the scientists and space engineers of the future.
